source.reason: Describes how the polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys (including the nominal 7 at.% Al alloy) were produced: vacuum induction melting and solidification in Cu moulds to 18 mm rods; the as-cast state is the sample condition.

method.value: vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles followed by solidification in Cu moulds

processing_steps_notes.value: Binary Fe-Al alloy with nominal 7 at.% Al; prepared from Fe of 99.99% purity (purified by zone melting to minimise impurity content) and Al of 99.999% purity; cast into rods usually 18 mm in diameter. The alloy is used in the as-cast condition, i.e. without any subsequent heat treatment (real Al and C contents of the nominal Fe-7%Al alloy were not determined, Table 1).

source.reason: Specimen preparation for the mechanical/hardness tests applies to the specimens including the as-cast polycrystalline samples.

method.value: specimens cut by electrostatic discharge machining, mechanically polished and cleansed by ultrasound in acetone

processing_steps_notes.value: No heat treatment was applied to the as-cast sample; heat treatments described in the paper (up to 600 °C, 1100 °C etc.) pertain to other sample conditions, not to this as-cast sample.

source.reason: Microstructure of the as-cast polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys: coarse grains of order 1 mm and no second phases in the as-cast condition; ordering (K-state) only begins at about 10 at.% Al, so the 7 at.% Al matrix is a disordered bcc solid solution.

overall_structure.value: Polycrystalline as-cast alloy with a coarse grain structure; the as-cast alloys contained no second phases.

source.reason: The polycrystalline alloys with Al contents 4-18% (which include the nominal 7 at.% Al alloy) showed a coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm.
The as-cast alloys contained no second phases; only slow cooling/prolonged annealing produced grain-boundary carbides, which are therefore absent in the as-cast condition of this sample.

interface_notes.value: In the as-cast condition the polycrystalline alloy contained no second phases and the grain boundaries were free of the fine thin platelike or rod-like (carbide) precipitates that appear only after slow furnace cooling from 1100 °C or prolonged heat treatments (e.g. 14 days at 320 °C).

unmapped_findings: Fe-7%Al nominal composition: the real Al content and the C (carbon) content were not determined (n.d.) in Table 1, so the actual composition and impurity level of this specific alloy are unreported. [b0025]

The polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys with Al contents 4-18 at.% (the series that includes the nominal 7 at.% Al alloy) all had coarse grain structures of the order of 1 mm and contained no second phases in the as-cast condition. [b0022]

The observed room-temperature yield-stress increase with Al content corresponds to a solid-solution hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa for polycrystalline alloys with 0-18% Al (not sensitive to deformation rate or temperature), which is described by Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys; this contrasts with ~1 GPa reported for monocrystals. [b0058]

For the as-cast polycrystalline alloys, the ductility (elongation before necking and fracture strain) decreases with increasing Al content: ductile fracture for Al contents up to about 15 at.% Al at room temperature and up to about 12 at.% Al at -100 °C, with a transition to brittle fracture without necking in the range 15-18 at.% Al at room temperature and 12-14 at.% Al at -100 °C. The nominal 7 at.% Al alloy lies in the ductile regime. [b0059, b0070]
At -100 °C the tensile yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the as-cast polycrystalline alloys are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa. [b0038]

The tensile yield stress of the as-cast polycrystalline alloys equals that measured in compression at the same rate and temperature, and the ultimate tensile strength parallels the yield stress. [b0038]
